findings.quote: The council recently underwent its first inspection by the Regulator of Social Housing in August 2025, resulting in a C2 consumer grade, published in November 2025. The council has begun developing action plans to address these issues as part of its ongoing housing improvement programme.

findings.paper_title: Corporate Risk Register
findings.headline: Finance system Unit4 requires enhancements to ensure timely and accurate reporting following April 2023 implementation
findings.detail: The council's finance system, implemented April 2023, remains functionally deficient for decision support. A dedicated project manager with Unit4 experience has been employed to implement enhancements, with completion targeted at April 2027. Support contract renewed with new supplier. An internal steering group oversees the enhancement programme.
findings.matters: Weak financial reporting and budgeting systems undermine governance, audit confidence, and the reliability of financial information lenders and the council's own management depend on.
findings.figures: Completion target April 2027. Temporary project manager deployed. Priorities identified for implementation.
findings.quote: The Council's finance system, Unit4, requires enhancements following implementation in April 2023 to ensure that financial information is timely and accurate to support decision making.

findings.paper_title: Corporate Risk Register
findings.headline: Medium-term funding gap driven by government funding cuts and business rates uncertainty
findings.detail: The council faces a structural funding gap from reduced government funding, increased service demand, and high pay inflation. The 2025 consultations on business rates retention and fair funding review suggest significant potential losses in business rates growth to the council. The Provisional Finance Settlement 2026/27 provides three-year certainty allowing balanced budgets, but the underlying medium-term pressure remains unresolved.
findings.matters: Structural funding gaps and government funding uncertainty are primary credit concerns for lenders to local government.
findings.figures: Residual risk score 4 out of 16. Three-year balanced budget position confirmed in Provisional Finance Settlement 2026/27, with capacity to build reserves.
findings.quote: Reduced funding from Government. Increased demand for services, coupled with high inflation and pay awards has led to a funding gap over the medium term. The Council's consultations in respect of Business Rates Retention and the Fair Funding Review issued in 2025, suggest that the Council may face significant losses in terms of business rates growth.

findings.paper_title: General Fund Finance Update - 2025/26 Quarter 2 Cabinet Report
findings.headline: Prior inflation has eroded real purchasing power of reserves, compounding the effect of 44% annual drawdown
findings.detail: The council explicitly identifies that prior high inflation has permanently reduced the real value of its reserve balances. The council states this erosion of purchasing power 'poses a challenge to the organisation's ability to maintain financial stability and achieve its long-term financial objectives.' This impact is particularly significant given that the council is simultaneously drawing down reserves at 44% annually to fund capital programmes.
findings.matters: Reserves are being depleted quantitatively (£9.6m this year) while also being eroded qualitatively (inflation reducing what money can buy). This double compression of reserves reduces financial buffers faster than the headline numbers suggest, affecting the council's ability to sustain itself through future financial pressures.
findings.figures: 44% annual reserve depletion plus unnamed but acknowledged erosion from prior inflation impact
findings.quote: Although inflation has decreased, the impact of the high inflation means the real purchasing power of the Council's reserves steadily erodes, meaning the same amount of money can purchase progressively fewer goods and services. This erosion of value poses a challenge to the organisation's ability to maintain financial stability and achieve its long-term financial objectives.

findings.paper_title: General Fund Finance Update - 2025/26 Quarter 2 Cabinet Report
findings.headline: Finance system backlog prevented detailed Q2 analysis, limiting financial reporting to major variances only
findings.detail: The council was unable to complete detailed financial analysis for Q2 2025/26 due to a backlog in the finance system and delays in closing the 2024/25 Statement of Accounts. This forced Q2 reporting to be limited to discussion of major variances only, based on available information and discussions with budget holders, rather than comprehensive variance analysis. The 2024/25 accounts remain unclosed at the reporting date.
findings.matters: Finance system backlogs and delayed account closure create governance and transparency concerns. For external lenders assessing the council's financial position, incomplete reporting reduces the ability to assess full financial health and suggests strain on finance function capacity.
findings.figures: Q2 2025/26 reporting limited to major variances; 2024/25 accounts closure delayed beyond Q2 reporting date
findings.quote: Due to finance system backlog and delays in closing the 2024/25 accounts, detailed analysis was not possible; therefore, only major variances are reported based on available information and discussions with Finance and budget holders.

findings.paper_title: General Fund Finance Update - 2025/26 Quarter 2 Cabinet Report
findings.headline: Usable reserves declining by £9.6m (44% of opening balance) through strategic capital funding drawdowns
findings.detail: General Fund usable reserves are forecast to fall from £21.9m at 1 April 2025 to £12.2m at 31 March 2026—a reduction of £9.6m or 44% of opening reserves in a single financial year. This is driven by the council's strategy to draw down earmarked reserves to fund capital programmes, particularly the MTFP reserve (£8.3m reduction) and Business Rates reserve (£549k reduction), reducing available financial buffers substantially.
findings.matters: Consuming 44% of reserves in one year to fund capital significantly erodes financial flexibility and the council's capacity to absorb economic shocks or service demand spikes, affecting creditworthiness and long-term sustainability.
findings.figures: Opening reserves £21.853m, closing forecast £12.214m, total drawdown £9.638m (44%), MTFP reserve reduction £8.332m
findings.quote: There is a significant reduction in the business rates reserve, this is due to the Council's strategy of utilising reserves to fund the capital programme.

findings.paper_title: General Fund Finance Update - 2025/26 Quarter 2 Cabinet Report
findings.headline: £7.5m vehicle fleet procurement delays reduce capital programme spending to 27% of budget
findings.detail: The General Fund capital programme has a revised budget of £10.9m for 2025/26, but forecast outturn is only £3m (27% of budget), with £7.9m slipping into future years. The majority of the slippage, £7.5m, is specifically due to delays in procuring specialist vehicles for the fleet replacement programme. Actual spending to September was only £905k (8% of budget), indicating significant execution shortfalls.
findings.matters: Capital programme delivery shortfalls of 73% indicate potential procurement challenges and project execution risk. This signals whether the council can deliver essential services and affects future capital planning credibility.
findings.figures: Budget £10.904m, forecast outturn £3.020m, slippage £7.913m (with £7.499m specifically in vehicle fleet procurement)
findings.quote: The majority of the slippage, £7.5m, into 2026/27, is due to the long lead time in procuring specialist vehicles within the fleet replacement programme.

findings.paper_title: Housing Revenue Account (HRA) Finance Update - 2025/26 Quarter 2 Cabinet Report
findings.headline: Council preparing response plan following recent Regulator of Social Housing inspection outcome.
findings.detail: Listed as part of HRA service improvement work, the council is "Preparing a plan for further actions within the service in response to the recent Regulator of Social Housing inspection outcome," indicating the inspection identified matters requiring action.
findings.matters: RSH inspections assess compliance and performance of social housing providers. A lender needs to understand whether regulatory concerns exist about the council's HRA management, service delivery, or compliance.

findings.quote: Preparing a plan for further actions within the service in response to the recent Regulator of Social Housing inspection outcome.

findings.paper_title: Housing Revenue Account (HRA) Finance Update - 2025/26 Quarter 2 Cabinet Report
findings.headline: Finance system backlog prevents detailed HRA financial analysis; only major variances reported based on budget holder discussions.
findings.detail: The council states that delays in closing 2024/25 accounts and finance system backlog have made detailed analysis impossible, limiting the scope of this quarterly report to major variances discussed between finance team and budget holders.
findings.matters: A lender requires confidence that the council can track, control, and report on financial position accurately and in real time. Inability to perform detailed analysis is a governance weakness that obscures risk visibility.
findings.figures: None
findings.quote: Due to finance system backlog and delays in closing the 2024/25 accounts, detailed analysis was not possible; therefore, only major variances are reported, based on available information and discussions between the finance team and budget holders.

findings.paper_title: Housing Revenue Account (HRA) Finance Update - 2025/26 Quarter 2 Cabinet Report
findings.headline: Multiple capital projects slipping due to internal resource constraints in procurement and capital delivery.
findings.detail: Sheltered scheme improvements slipping £0.3m and scheme lighting slipping £0.2m because "internal resource not being able to complete the procurement process and deliver works onsite." Fleet replacement programme also delayed awaiting vehicle acquisition.
findings.matters: Capital programme delays due to internal resourcing shortages signal risk to delivery of the medium-term capital plan. For a lender, this raises questions about whether the council has sufficient staffing to execute its investment ambitions.
findings.figures: Sheltered slippage £300k, lighting slippage £200k, fleet slippage £100k
findings.quote: Sheltered scheme improvements with a budget of £0.7m and nil spend to date. This is predicted to slip £0.3m into future years due to internal resource not being able to complete the procurement process and deliver works onsite.

findings.paper_title: Housing Revenue Account (HRA) Finance Update - 2025/26 Quarter 2 Cabinet Report
findings.headline: £380k forecast overspend on repairs and maintenance to clear a historic backlog of work-in-progress and outstanding repairs.
findings.detail: The council is commissioning contractors to assist in delivering against repairs backlogs as part of broader HRA service improvement. This overspend is being absorbed in the overall HRA forecast.
findings.matters: The scale of maintenance backlog requiring investment signals asset condition issues and understaffed internal delivery. For a lender, this affects understanding of the housing stock's true state and the council's capacity to manage it.
findings.figures: £380k overspend
findings.quote: £380k forecast overspend on repairs and maintenance, primarily reflecting progress made in addressing historic work-in-progress and outstanding repairs.

findings.paper_title: Housing Revenue Account (HRA) Finance Update - 2025/26 Quarter 2 Cabinet Report
findings.headline: HRA capital programme forecast to spend £17.2m against revised budget of £14.9m, representing 115% spend and £2.3m overspend.
findings.detail: The New Supply programme accounts for much of this, forecasting £5.2m spend against a £2.3m budget (£2.9m overspend). The council states this overspend will be covered by budget slippage from previous years. Contributing factors include S106 development delays and delivery partner delays outside direct council control.
findings.matters: A lender needs confidence in capital spending trajectory and adequacy of resources. Spending at 115% of budget signals acceleration and reliance on prior-year flexibility rather than current-year funding.
findings.figures: £14.9m budget, £17.2m forecast outturn; New Supply £2.3m budget vs £5.2m forecast
findings.quote: The revised 2025/26 budget for the Active Programme HRA Capital Programme is £14.9m. Actual spend at the end of Quarter 2 was £1. 4m and forecast outturn is £17.2m, representing 115% of the revised budget resulting in £2.3m overspend which will be covered by budget slippage from previous years.

findings.paper_title: Medium Term Financial Plan 2025 - 2028 Cabinet Report
findings.headline: Net zero carbon targets may require significant capital investment and project reprioritisation
findings.detail: The council is assessing the financial implications of meeting net zero carbon targets. These are likely to require substantial capital investment, which may force reprioritisation of other capital projects.
findings.matters: Unquantified capital commitments for net zero add to the council's budget pressure; if the costs are material, the council may be forced to defer other capital priorities.
findings.figures: Assessment underway
findings.quote: The Council is also assessing the financial implications of meeting net zero carbon targets, which may require significant capital investment and reprioritisation of projects.

findings.paper_title: Medium Term Financial Plan 2025 - 2028 Cabinet Report
findings.headline: Fair Funding Review outcomes not confirmed until December 2025, creating budget planning uncertainty
findings.detail: The government's Fair Funding Review will significantly impact council funding, but outcomes are not expected until mid/late December 2025. This timing forces the council to either budget with incomplete information or revise draft proposals after publication.
findings.matters: Late government notification of funding changes forces budgets to be prepared with incomplete information, increasing execution risk and requiring emergency revisions.
findings.figures: Outcomes expected December 2025
findings.quote: As the Provisional Finance Settlement is not expected to be announced until mid/late December (as has been the case in previous years), it is challenging to produce draft proposals in time for Cabinet to consider them prior to being published for consultation.

findings.paper_title: Medium Term Financial Plan 2025 - 2028 Cabinet Report
findings.headline: Named government grants are being reduced or phased out
findings.detail: The council has depended on New Homes Bonus, Minimum Funding Guarantee, Extended Producer Responsibility payments, and National Insurance Contributions Grant. The council explicitly states these grants are being reduced or phased out, adding to financial uncertainty.
findings.matters: Loss of specific grant streams narrows the funding base available to balance budgets without service cuts or borrowing.
findings.figures: New Homes Bonus, Minimum Funding Guarantee, Extended Producer Responsibility payments, National Insurance Contributions Grant
findings.quote: Grants such as the New Homes Bonus, Minimum Funding Guarantee, Extended Producer Responsibility payments, and National Insurance Contributions Grant have supported our finances. However, many of these are being reduced or phased out, adding to the uncertainty.

findings.paper_title: Medium Term Financial Plan 2025 - 2028 Cabinet Report
findings.headline: Business rates reset in 2026/27 likely to reduce council income significantly
findings.detail: Business rates growth has been the council's main source of financial stability, funding both day-to-day services and capital. The planned reset in 2026/27 will reduce income, and the Fair Funding Review may redistribute resources to other authorities. The exact impact is unknown until December 2025.
findings.matters: If business rates fall sharply, the council loses a major, relatively stable income stream with little flexibility to recover, forcing either service cuts or borrowing.
findings.figures: Business rates reset 2026/27; Fair Funding Review outcomes December 2025
findings.quote: the planned business rates reset in 2026/27 is likely to reduce the Council's income, and the Fair Funding Review may redistribute resources to other authorities.

findings.paper_title: Medium Term Financial Plan 2025 - 2028 Cabinet Report
findings.headline: Base funding gap of £578k in 2026/27 growing to £1.6m in 2027/28, worst case £4.3m
findings.detail: The council's sensitivity analysis shows a base-case funding gap of £578k in 2026/27 and £1.6m in 2027/28. In a worst case, the gap could reach £4.3m in 2026/27. The council plans to address this through a transformation programme, departmental savings, and income maximisation, but the specifics are not yet detailed.
findings.matters: A £1.6m gap in 2027/28 signals the council will need material spending cuts or income increases; a lender would need confidence the council has identified credible savings without depleting reserves unsustainably.
findings.figures: £578k in 2026/27, £1.6m in 2027/28, worst case £4.3m in 2026/27, projected gap of £2.6m by 2028/29
findings.quote: The base case shows a funding gap of £578k in 2026/27 and £1.6m in 2027/28. The worst case could see the gap widen to £4.3m in 2026/27 due to reduced funding and increased costs.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Auditor's Annual Report - 2023/24 and 2024/25
findings.headline: Internal Audit has issued a limited assurance opinion for both years, with 36 high and 31 medium-priority recommendations outstanding.
findings.detail: The council's internal audit service (shared with two other councils) issued a limited assurance opinion for 2023/24 and 2024/25. In 2024/25 alone, 36 high and 31 medium recommendations were raised. A large number of recommendations from 2023/24 remained outstanding, primarily because they relate to Unit 4 system issues that could not be remedied.
findings.matters: Limited assurance from internal audit means the council's internal control environment is not functioning effectively. The sheer number of high-priority recommendations (36) suggests material control gaps. Inability to implement recommendations due to systems issues indicates the control environment will remain weak until Unit 4 is stabilised.
findings.figures: 2024/25 high-priority recommendations: 36. Medium-priority: 31. Prior year recommendations outstanding: substantial number still unresolved.
findings.quote: The Head of Internal Audit has issued a limited assurance opinion for the years 2023/24 and 2024/25. During 2024/25 Internal Audit raised 36 high and 31 medium recommendations.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Auditor's Annual Report - 2023/24 and 2024/25
findings.headline: Local Government Reorganisation creates medium-term strategic uncertainty; council ceases April 2028.
findings.detail: The council is being absorbed into a new unitary authority on 1 April 2028. This creates significant risks: uncertainty about senior staff retention, potential for reserves to be repurposed by successor body, distraction of management time from delivering current savings plans, and questions about governance and reserve stewardship during the transition period.
findings.matters: For a lender, reorganisation creates uncertainty about the entity's ongoing viability and management quality during the transition. There is also explicit risk that the council's accumulated reserves (£15.25m general fund, projected to grow significantly) could be diverted to cover overruns by the successor unitary authority.
findings.figures: Council transition date: 1 April 2028. General fund reserves 31 March 2024: £15.25m. Projected 31 March 2028: £29.78m. Projected 31 March 2030: £38.59m.
findings.quote: There may be an incentive for more short-term decision making in respect of the use of reserves and concerns, where reserves have been built up over previous years, either via strong management or for the implementation of a particular redevelopment scheme, that these reserves may end up being repurposed to cover an overspend incurred by a successor body.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Auditor's Annual Report - 2023/24 and 2024/25
findings.headline: Medium-term funding gaps of £578k (2026/27) and £1,616k (2027/28) to be addressed by savings plans.
findings.detail: The council's latest draft MTFS shows funding shortfalls requiring savings programmes. For 2025/26, £599k of savings were targeted, with only £19k achieved by Q1 and £53k identified as at risk of non-delivery. The council is planning savings for 2026/27 and 2027/28 but has not yet finalised how these will be achieved.
findings.matters: Funding gaps with unproven savings plans create deficit risk. The fact that some 2025/26 savings are already at risk of non-delivery suggests the council may struggle to close future gaps, particularly given the distraction of the LGR transition.
findings.figures: 2025/26 savings target: £599k. Achieved by Q1: £19k. At risk: £53k. Projected gaps 2026/27: £578k. 2027/28: £1,616k.
findings.quote: The latest draft MTFS identifies funding gaps in 26/27 and 27/28 of £578k and £1,616k respectively. At Q1 2025/26 £19k had been achieved and the Council reported being on track to deliver a further £527k of savings by the year end. We note that £53k of savings identified were reported as at risk of non delivery in Q1.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Auditor's Annual Report - 2023/24 and 2024/25
findings.headline: Material gaps in financial planning communication: additional Unit 4 costs not communicated to members beyond May 2024.
findings.detail: The auditors found that while Unit 4 costs escalated from the original £633k + £300k approved budget to £997k+ by May 2024, there is no evidence that additional costs beyond May 2024 have been communicated to members. The Section 151 Officer's communication to the Audit Committee Chair in May 2024 did not fully communicate the severity, extent or impact of Unit 4 issues. Cabinet updates on Unit 4 stopped after September 2022.
findings.matters: Lenders need accurate and timely information about cost overruns and control weaknesses. Lack of transparency to the council's own audit committee and cabinet suggests governance failures and raises questions about what else may not be communicated.
findings.figures: Latest documented spend: £997k as of May 2024. No final cost figures provided.
findings.quote: we have reviewed papers presented to subsequent cabinet meetings until September 2025 and have not identified any other update provided by management to members. However, it is our view, that this communication did not fully communicate the severity, extent or the impact of the issues experienced with the implementation of Unit 4 ERPx.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Auditor's Annual Report - 2023/24 and 2024/25
findings.headline: Three significant weaknesses identified in council's arrangements for value for money; governance is most severe.
findings.detail: The auditors have identified significant weaknesses in governance arrangements, specifically around decision-making on major projects (Unit 4), communication to members, and risk management. Weaknesses relate to absence of documented options appraisals for the Unit 4 system decision, lack of transparency about costs and delays to members, and failure to record Unit 4 risks on the corporate risk register initially.
findings.matters: Governance weaknesses indicate the council's decision-making and risk management processes are not fit for purpose. This raises questions about the reliability of other major decisions and the council's ability to manage risks effectively.
findings.figures: 3 key recommendations made in respect of governance. 2 other recommendations relating to financial sustainability and efficiency.
findings.quote: we do consider that significant weaknesses exist in the Council's arrangements for governance and how the body ensures that it makes informed decisions and properly manages its risks.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Auditor's Annual Report - 2023/24 and 2024/25
findings.headline: Finance team operating at critical capacity with heavy reliance on agency staff, creating sustainability risk.
findings.detail: The council has experienced severe capacity challenges in its finance team, exacerbated by the delays in implementing the new ledger system. The team is heavily dependent on agency staff. There is a significant risk that agency staff involved in the Unit 4 implementation could leave at short notice, causing loss of corporate memory. While the council is recruiting permanent staff (Finance Team Manager, systems accountant, LGA Graduate), the team remains below sustainable levels.
findings.matters: High agency reliance and understaffing create continuity risk in financial reporting and controls. Loss of key staff during the reorganisation period (leading to unitary authority April 2028) could worsen delays in financial reporting and account production.
findings.figures: Internal audit raised 36 high and 31 medium recommendations in 2024/25; many from 2023/24 remained outstanding due to Unit 4 issues.
findings.quote: The finance team has experienced capacity concerns and has a high level of dependency on agency staff. There is a further risk that these staff who have been involved with the implementation of Unit4 ERPx could leave at short notice, potentially losing corporate memory.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Auditor's Annual Report - 2023/24 and 2024/25
findings.headline: Unit 4 financial system implementation has caused massive delays in account production and cost overruns, with known bugs still unresolved.
findings.detail: The council's ledger system replacement project, awarded to Embridge in December 2020 with a go-live target of Autumn 2021, was switched mid-implementation to an undeveloped cloud-based version (ERPx). The 2023/24 accounts were not produced until August 2025 (missing the 28 February 2025 deadline), and 2024/25 accounts are not expected until end November 2025 (missing the 31 May 2025 deadline). The project has cost at least £997k by May 2024 against an original approved budget of £633k plus £300k contingency. Bank reconciliations and other key financial procedures still require manual workarounds due to system bugs.
findings.matters: Delayed accounts mean lenders cannot get timely financial information. Unresolved control weaknesses in the financial system create material audit risk. The cost overruns and implementation failure indicate governance failures in project management and decision-making.
findings.figures: Original budget £633k, approved additional £300k, actual spend £997k by May 2024. 2023/24 accounts production delayed 6 months (to August 2025). 2024/25 accounts delayed 6 months (to end November 2025).
findings.quote: The Council was unable to produce the 2023/24 statement of accounts until August 2025, thereby missing the national backstop deadline for the publication of audited accounts by 28 February 2025. The 2024/25 statement of accounts are expected to be produced by the end of November 2025, which is significantly delayed beyond the statutory deadline of 31 May 2025.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Auditor's Annual Report - 2023/24 and 2024/25
findings.headline: Auditor unable to sign off either year's financial statements due to backstop deadline.
findings.detail: The auditors intend to disclaim their audit report for both 2023/24 and 2024/25, meaning the financial statements have not been independently verified as presenting a true and fair view. For 2023/24, the draft accounts arrived after the statutory deadline of 28 February 2025. For 2024/25, the auditors do not expect to complete sufficient work before the 27 February 2026 backstop date.
findings.matters: Lenders rely on independently audited accounts to assess financial position and creditworthiness. An audit disclaimer means the council's financial position cannot be verified as reliable.
findings.figures: 2024/25 backstop deadline: 27 February 2026. 2023/24 backstop deadline: 28 February 2025.
findings.quote: Due to the challenges of undertaking an audit where previous years have been 'disclaimed' because of the local authority backstop, it has not been possible to regain full assurance. It is therefore not possible to for us to undertake sufficient work for 2024/25 to support an unmodified audit opinion ahead of the backstop date of 27 February 2026.

news_drafts.headline: North West Leicestershire flags housing account sustainability risk as reserves fall
news_drafts.lead: North West Leicestershire's housing account faces sustainability risks as unrestricted reserves—money the council can actually spend—fall to critical levels, the council warned this week. Reserves stand at £1.688m, only 68% above the statutory minimum of £1.000m. Consecutive years of financial pressure have driven this decline, with operating expenditure, the cost of day-to-day running, exceeding forecast by £0.293m in the first quarter of 2026/27 alone. Maintenance costs are running £1.022m over budget due to increased repairs activity and £0.204m in compensation for historic repair failures. The council has cut planned debt repayment by 27%, from £1.319m to £1.000m, to manage the pressure, while allocating £0.735m to building reserves.

news_drafts.headline: Housing account faces new year operating pressure despite debt repayment plans
news_drafts.lead: North West Leicestershire's housing revenue account, which manages the council's own rented homes, is forecast to overspend on day-to-day running costs by £293,000 in its first quarter, the second consecutive year of such pressure. The council had budgeted to repay £1.319m of borrowing this year but has cut that to £1m, citing financial pressure on the account. The overspend is driven by higher-than-expected repair and maintenance costs—£1.022m above budget—particularly on in-house repairs, heating systems, asbestos work and compensation for historic repair failures. The council is partly offsetting the pressure through an interest income windfall of £295,000 from favourable rates. Despite the setback, the council plans to allocate its net operating surplus of £1.735m between the £1m debt repayment and £735,000 towards rebuilding general reserves, which stood at only £1.688m at the end of March.
